findings.summary: The docs say the dry run answers the run's exit code for the same failure, which does not hold for an invalid sync-state file: the run fails before the pass with exit 1, while the dry run never checks the sync-state and answers 0.
evidence: sync_cards.go:192-194 SyncCardsProject calls w.checkSyncState() first and returns OtherFailure (exit 1).
sync_cards.go:74-88 and app.go:152-158 PlanCards and planCards never call checkSyncState.
cmd_sync.go:96-103 maps the dry-run error with syncExitCode(promote.CardRunFailure(err)); the run uses the same mapping at cmd_sync.go:135 and sync_cards.go:198.
sync_memorycard_test.go:260-355 pins exits 4, 6 and 5 with stdout, stderr and vault checks.
sync_source_golden_test.go:18-41 and testdata/sync-source-golden/01-04 hold args, exit, stdout, stderr and the full vault tree.
app.go:111-120 and engram_degraded.go:31-37 announce degraded opens on stderr only when degraded; tests at sync_memorycard_test.go:383-411.
app.go:122-128 closeStore only warns on stderr and cannot change an exit code; plain sync keeps defer store.Close() at cmd_sync.go:56.
